_doc: Book questions the coordinate parser cannot recover, transcribed BY EYE from the rendered pages of docs/Radiokomunikacije_ocr.pdf. The answer still comes from the book's own key table (book_keys.json) — only the question text and the option ORDER are supplied here, since the key is read by position a/b/c/d. Page numbers are PDF pages; the printed page is 5 higher.

_reasons.merged-block: Two questions ran together into one block because neither carried an OCR'd number, so the parser could not see the boundary.
_reasons.stacked-options: All four options are set in a single full-width column rather than two, which the column logic reads as stem continuation.
_reasons.figure-options: The options ARE diagrams; there is no option text in the source at all.
_reasons.cross-reference: The options are bare letters referring to the figure of an earlier question.
_reasons.figure-in-stem: The question parses fine on its own, but a sketch sits between the stem and the options and the sketch's own printed label sat in the stem's x-column, so the coordinate parser stitched it onto the stem as if it were wrapped text. The question text here replaces that reading; the options are unchanged from what the parser already found.
_reasons.figure-plain: A schematic, curve or oscillogram sits between the stem and the options. The coordinate parser read the stem and options correctly on its own -- no text was glued together -- so only the crop window is added here, nothing is patched.
_reasons.stem-split-column: The stem's own text is set in two side-by-side columns at the same y (not stacked lines); the coordinate parser kept only the first column and silently dropped the second. Nothing from a figure bled in -- this restores the stem's own missing half.
